results.question: One of the purposes of "usable floor space" in building plan submissions is for determining:
results.responseText:
Option A is supported. PNAP APP-35 states that the **size of a refuse chamber (RC)** “should be based on the **TUFS** of each domestic building or domestic part of a composite building” and then gives RC size ranges by TUFS bands [PNAP APP-35: Refuse Storage and Collection (BD), current, Appendix C item (iii)]. Since TUFS means total usable floor space, usable floor space is expressly used for determining the area/size of the refuse chamber [PNAP APP-35: Refuse Storage and Collection (BD), current, Appendix C item (iii)].

Option D is not the best answer. The Fire Safety Code uses **usable floor area** for assessing **occupant capacity** in certain cases, e.g. “the usable floor area for assessing the occupant capacity in the swimming pool…” [Code of Practice for Fire Safety in Buildings (BD), 2011 (2024 Edition), Section 2 – Provisions of Means of Escape, note 5]. That relates to means of escape calculations, but the question asks for one purpose of “usable floor space” in building plan submissions; the clearest direct planning/submission use shown in the retrieved regulations is RC sizing by TUFS. Options B and C are not supported by the retrieved text: no retrieved sanitary-fitment provision ties the requirement to “usable floor space,” and no retrieved regulation defines it as simply the area within a flat exclusive of common areas.

The answer is A
